content.comment_body: Just tried downloading the latest [product_name] version [version_no] (v8.2), but the installer isn't recognizing my previous setup ([version_no] V8.1.1) and keeps saying 'not qualified'. I installed the original software from the DVD ([version_no] v8.0), then tried updating to [version_no] v8.2, but the same error appears, even when selecting the folder directly from the DVD. I never had such issues with [version_no] V8.1.1. Has anyone else encountered this or found a solution?
I've installed several versions of [product_name] on my PC and all have worked fine: - [version_no] V6.1.12 - [version_no] V7.1.5 - [version_no] V8.0 - [version_no] V8.1.1 - [version_no] V8.2
I forgot to mention—I'm trying to install [version_no] v8.2 on macOS. The update works on my PC, so it looks like something specifically fails during the update on macOS.
If I were in your situation, I'd consider submitting a support request.
I'll do that if necessary. Is there anything new in [version_no] V8.2?

Here are the new features in [product_name] [version_no] V8.2: - Go online function for scanning [product_name] Operator Device (TDE) in network mode - Online/offline settings for [product_name] Operator Device (TDE) - Updated flag colors: M8 (Initialization Flag, blue), M27 (Message Character Set Flag, green) in [product_name] For [product_name] Access Tool V2.0.0: - Set data synchronization period - View historical data - Start or stop data synchronization For details, see the [product_name] Access Tool Help. Also, [product_name] Web Editor (a new tool for use with [product_name] Basis Module and [product_name]) allows you to: - Create user-defined web pages - View the entire project via the Web Server on the [product_name] Basis Module For more, refer to the [document] for [product_name] Web Editor.
The correct upgrade file for [version_no] V8.2 for Windows 32-bit is now available for download.

After trying for several evenings, I solved the installation issue! I had an old Java version (Java 6). Upgrading to the latest Java 8 (151) let me install [product_name] [version_no] V8.2 with no problem. Mac users: update Java to version 8 and it should work.

Thanks! I suspected Java was the cause and you confirmed it. I even wiped my MacBook and upgraded to Mojave. Reinstalled [product_name] v8—it wanted the legacy Java version, so it seemed sorted. Then I installed v8.2, which needs the latest Java—totally unexpected. The support page should be updated with this info. Thanks again!

analysis.insight_summary: Users faced installation problems with [product_name] [version_no] V8.2 on macOS, where previous installations weren't detected and a 'not qualified' error appeared. The root cause was using outdated Java (Java 6) rather than the required Java 8 or newer. Windows installs worked without trouble, but macOS required manual Java updates. Incomplete guidance from support resources heightened user frustration.
analysis.user_expectations: Users want a smooth upgrade process for [product_name] on both macOS and Windows, with clear error explanations and current support documentation detailing system requirements.
